Exception Worklist

Every MRP and policy exception as a work item: review it, assign an owner, comment, snooze or close. Closed items stay closed until the situation changes.

Rough-Cut Capacity

Load per work center by week from work orders and MRP planned orders, on the routing standard, against available hours on the plant calendar. Excess an alternate line can take is shown, not flagged.

Finite Scheduling

Production orders are placed on work centers against real hours, the plant calendar, component availability, labor and tools. Setups follow the changeover matrix, steps can overlap, and busy lines spill to alternates. Latest start comes from a finite backward pass.

Scheduling rules

Routings

Hours = setup + run × order qty (incl. assembly scrap). Setup applies after a different family; same-family setup applies after the same family. Transfer qty > 0 lets the next operation start after the first batch (overlap). Move days = wait before the next operation when there is no overlap.

Labor and tools

A routing step that needs a technician or fixture can only run while one is free, even if the work center is idle. Use pools for crews (TECH x2) and tools for fixtures, stencils or test heads.

Changeover matrix

Hours to change a work center from one family to another. Missing pairs use the routing setup.

Requisitions and Approvals

Planned orders and policy buys become purchase requisitions. Spend limits route each one to the right approver before it becomes a PO.

Spend approval limits

At or below the planner limit, requisitions are approved automatically. Only a Manager can change limits.

Team roles

Audit Trail

Every change, approval, confirmation and sync conflict. Each entry is hashed together with the author's previous entry (SHA-256), so editing or deleting an entry in the middle is detected.

Stock Status and Availability

Physical stock split into usable, held and reserved, plus open supply. Each unit is counted once.

Stock overview by item

Usable = Physical − Quality hold − Blocked Available = Usable − Reservations Inventory position = Usable + Open orders − Backorders Days of supply = Usable ÷ Avg daily usage

Open purchase and work orders

Open = Ordered − Received − Canceled. Planning uses the supplier promise date; without one the line is Unconfirmed and stays out of the committed plan. A line past its promise date is Overdue and is not counted until re-promised. Usable = promise date + inspection days on the plant calendar.

Batches and shelf life

Unrestricted stock by batch for shelf-life items. Demand uses the earliest use-by date first (FEFO). Use-by = expiry (SLED) minus the item's minimum remaining life. Quantity left at use-by shows as expiring stock in MRP.

Reservations (dated)

Each reservation is a requirement in the week of its date, counted once.

Supplier delivery performance

Slip = working days between requested and promised date. On-time = promised on or before requested.

Demand Planning and Forecast Accuracy

Backtest each method, pick the lowest error, and send the finished good forecast to MRP.

Order promising (available-to-promise)

Method settings

Actuals vs one-step-ahead forecasts

Backtest detail

Error = Actual − Forecast (positive = underforecast). MAPE skips zero-actual months and reports how many were excluded.

Independent demand to MRP

Every MRP item can carry its own demand: finished goods and top-level items default to their statistical forecast; components default to none (turn on for spares or service demand).

Seasonal profile (index by month)

Weekly forecast = monthly forecast × 12 ÷ 52. Requirement = larger of forecast and customer orders, so orders consume the forecast instead of adding to it. With source None, only orders go to MRP.

MRP planning parameters (same item master)

Lot rules: L4L lot-for-lot · FIXED fixed lot size · MAX replenish to max stock · POQ period lot covering N weeks. MOQ and rounding apply to L4L, MAX and POQ. Safety stock blank = calculated from service level.

Clear-to-Build

How many units the material on hand and promised supply can support, and what limits the build.

Component availability by need date

Supported builds = FLOOR(Available ÷ Qty per) Shortage = MAX(0, Required − Available) Available = Usable − reservations due by the need week + promised receipts usable by the need week.

Shortage Recovery Options

Options are built from the actual shortage: same quantity, same need date. Each cost sits with the option that causes it.

Recovery options

Cost = Expedite freight + Premium × Qty + Setup + Overtime + Penalties + Downtime hrs × $/hr Recommendations are for planner review. Confirm approved part, supplier, usable date and any reservation release before acting.
